messages:
maria: Idea: introduce an 'activation_hold' lifecycle state for on-prem package rollouts — a short, operator-controllable pause between successful staging and final commit. Rationale: gives operators a chance to run checks or abort after long-running fetch/apply steps.

aj: How long is short? We should pick a safe default but allow per-component override. Also need clear semantics for auto-expiry: auto-commit vs auto-rollback.

simon: Failure modes to consider: node crash during hold, controller disagreement on state, and incomplete temp writes. Persist a pre-activation snapshot and an activation token so aborts are deterministic.

kevin: For multi-node: require quorum of 'ready' acknowledgements for shard owners before entering hold state. If quorum lost during hold, mark as degraded and refuse commit until re-sync.

olivia: Default TTL should be conservative (e.g. 90-180s). Document that long holds increase disk/GC pressure and may block subsequent rollouts. Provide visible counters in console.

maria: Config sketch:
{ "activation_hold_seconds": "120", "auto_commit_on_expiry": "false", "max_concurrent_holds": "3" }

aj: Important: keep it compatible with delta and seedless flows. If aborted, we should attempt fast rollback using staged ops rather than full re-download. Maintain an inverse apply plan for quick revert when possible.

simon: Security: signer metadata must include an activation TTL and nonce to prevent replayed activations. Verify signatures before transitioning to hold.

kevin: Rollback modes: quick-revert (use pre-apply snapshot + atomic rename) vs quarantine (mark pending and require manual cleanup). Quick-revert only when no irreversible actions (e.g., irreversible DB migrations) were taken.

olivia: UX: console needs extend/abort buttons per activation, batch controls, and audit logs. Also show which components are in hold and reasons.

maria: State machine recommendation: staged -> hold -> committing -> active OR staged -> hold -> aborted -> cleanup. Emit metrics: hold_count, hold_expiry_count, hold_extend_count.

aj: Implementation note: store activation marker locally: activation_marker=content_hash|seq|state|expires_at. Ensure commit idempotency by checking marker before commit.

simon: On disk: write staged files to .tmp/<package>/<seq>/ then atomic rename to final path on commit. Journal operations to allow deterministic rewind if abort.

kevin: API: add /v1/activation-holds listing + POST /extend and POST /abort endpoints. Require admin auth; rate-limit extend to avoid TTL spam.

olivia: Enterprise policy: allow cluster admins to raise default hold TTL or change auto_commit_on_expiry behaviour. Document SLO tradeoffs.

maria: CLI ideas: `redwoodctl activation hold extend --id <pkg> --seconds 300` and `redwoodctl activation hold abort --id <pkg> --force` (force requires MFA).

aj: Telemetry: when hold expires/auto-rolls, tag with reason (timeout, failed-healthcheck, operator-abort) so support and Optimize can spot patterns.

simon: I'll draft a compact activation journal layout and idempotency checks.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary job/8124 deployed activation-hold prototype to staging. Tests include extend/abort/auto-expiry.

kevin: Note: make the hold per-component (model shard, runtime, config) not global. Also support batch extend/abort for multi-component rollouts.

olivia: Agree. Also ensure clear messaging in console when multiple packages are blocked by long holds.

maria: Decisions: default hold 120s; default auto_commit_on_expiry=false; enforce quorum for shard activations; require signer TTL; provide CLI + console + audit + metrics.

maria: Action items:
- maria: draft RFC for activation_hold state and UX (due Wed)
- simon: activation journal spec + atomic apply/revert API (due Tue)
- aj: prototype redwoodctl hold subcommands and server endpoints (due Fri)
- kevin: define /v1/activation-holds API and metrics contract (due Fri)
- olivia: enterprise policy text + docs (due next Mon)

maria: tagging @kevin @aj @simon for arch review next week.

simon: SGTM, I'll start the journal PR.

aj: I'll spike the CLI and add e2e checks.

maria: Thanks everyone. Putting RFC on calendar.
